variants.label: V7 GPU identity — transparent artboard, source->wave-warp(height:0)->output
variants.assertion: PARTIAL -- NOT bin-for-bin identical to V3 (sha differs; alphaOpaque within 0.24% of V3's, alphaPartial 4351 vs V3's 2888, a 1463-pixel/0.16%-of-frame residual). The QUALITATIVE double-composite signature IS gone: pre-fix, topPartialAlphaValues clustered tightly around the values the 2a-a^2 formula predicts from V3's own antialiasing steps (191/0.749 -> ~239, matching the observed 232-243 cluster with counts 36-40 each, all near-saturating). Post-fix, the top values are scattered across many distinct alphas (254:54, 1:48, 247:43, 239:40, 251:40, 4:40, 11:37, 22:36) with no single dominant cluster and much lower per-value counts -- consistent with two INDEPENDENT SVG rasterizers (the browser's native Canvas2D decode for the base layer vs the GPU pass's own SVG-to-WebGL-texture upload for its source) anti-aliasing the same vector edge very slightly differently, not with a systematic compositing bias. This residual is a rasterizer-fidelity gap between two independent SVG rasterization pipelines, not the double-composite defect this task targeted -- STEP 3 (the compositing-operator fix) is confirmed working, but achieving true bit-identical V7==V3 would require unifying (or bit-matching) the GPU surface's own SVG-to-texture rasterization against Canvas2D's native SVG decode, which is out of this task's scope.
